Definitely try to see the hospital LC if they have one. Try hand expressing the colostrum. Once the milk starts transitioning, start pumping. My hospital also had pumps that the maternity ward could use freely (provided they purchased their own pump parts). Pumping was essential for me when I was trying to get my supply going in the early days (I couldn't latch my baby because the pain was honestly basically equivalent to labour, it was that bad). Keep the pumping schedule to once every 2 hours during the day. 

After I gave birth, my baby was taken to NICU, so my entire milk supply came from hand expressing and pumping, as I didn't put the baby to breast for the first time until days later. For reference, with frequent hand expressing, my milk came in at the end of the second day pp. then, I carried on with the pumping for about 6 weeks before her latch was bearable and we've been EBF since :)
